AWPTCM-T33317.objective:
• The policed-dscp map can be configured with mls qos map policed-dscp to remap bandwidth classes (green, yellow, red) to new-dscp, new-cos, new-queue and new-bandwidth-class values.
  • Policed-dscp map configuration appears in running-config and is preserved in startup-config after save and restart.
  • The policed-dscp map can be reverted to default using the "no mls qos map policed-dscp" command.
  • When a single-rate (or twin-rate) policer with action policed-dscp-transmit is applied (on switchport or static LAG), egress traffic in each bandwidth class is remarked according to the policed-dscp map.
  • Remarked packets (green/yellow/red) carry the new DSCP values defined in the map; packet counts match with no unexpected drops.
  • Configuration and remarking behavior is verified on switchport and static LAG interfaces.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.

Enable QoS. Configure mls qos map policed-dscp for a dscp value across bandwidth-classes (green to new-dscp/cos/queue/bandwidth-class etc.). Verify the map shows in running-config and show mls qos maps policed-dscp.
Save config, restart the DUT, and confirm the policed-dscp map is present in startup-config and after boot.
Use "no mls qos map policed-dscp ..." to remove the map entry and confirm it reverts to default.

Configure a policy-map with class default using police single-rate ... action policed-dscp-transmit. Apply to ingress switchport. Send traffic that exercises green/yellow/red. Verify on egress (capture + counters) that packets are remarked per the policed-dscp map with no drops.
Repeat the policer + policed-dscp-transmit on a static LAG interface. Confirm remarking works for the LAG.
Verify behavior for twin-rate policer variants if applicable.
